A1.justification: Both PDFs are readable throughout, including figures, equations, tables, and appendices. V2 explicitly identifies itself as an update of v1's original title. The substantial restructuring does not prevent reliable comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original transformer experiments on modular addition and asymmetric modular functions, together with sampling, embedding, loss, and architecture ablations in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: V2 reports original modular-arithmetic experiments, noiseless secret-recovery results, synthetic-task evaluations, and polynomial-sum experiments, including Tables 8, 12, and 20–21.

M1.justification: V2 drops v1's g_interval tail-augmentation component and f_inv sampling option. For addition, the loss changes from alpha R + (1-alpha)MSE with alpha=0.01 to alpha R + MSE with alpha=0.0001, retaining the radial penalty R. New adaptations include token embeddings for multiplication and variable-length decoder-only training without custom loss for synthetic tasks. The precise sparsity-weight revision is ambiguous because v2's zero-count formula conflicts with Figure 1.

E1.justification: V2 retains addition and asymmetric functions but adds noiseless secret recovery, modular multiplication, scalar products, copy, associative recall, parity, selective copy, and polynomial sums. Modulus coverage expands substantially, including additional composite moduli in Appendix A. V1's Appendix D reaches N=384; v2 retains N=256 experiments in Appendix A but does not retain the N=384 cases.

E2.justification: V1 Table 4 directly evaluates implementations of Gromov, Doshi, and Jelassi. V2 retains a Jelassi-style standard encoder baseline but removes the direct Gromov and Doshi MLP comparisons. It adds evaluated curriculum-learning comparisons in Table 4 and cross-entropy-loss comparisons in Table 22, substantially changing the comparator set.

E3.justification: The main configuration changes from 12 to 4 encoder layers, batch size 256 to 250, and learning rate 0.0001 to 0.00003. Training changes from 614.4M examples to 100M presentations of 10M distinct examples. Addition evaluation drops exact accuracy and the 0.3% tolerance, retaining 0.5% and adding 1%. New secret-recovery and sequence-output experiments introduce additional evaluation procedures.

E4.justification: Sparsity and easy-before-hard analyses are retained with revised experiments. V2 removes tail-augmentation, input/output embedding, and detailed internal-layer PCA analyses. It adds curriculum sensitivity, arbitrary padding-value tests, controlled example repetition, sample-efficiency comparisons, longer-training/larger-model tests, and MSE-versus-cross-entropy analysis. Appendix E newly examines loss-dependent collapse in noiseless secret recovery.

E5.justification: V1 Table 9 reports best/average/worst accuracy over four loss-ablation trials. That summary disappears. V2 Table 4 reports averages with ± quantities described as variance across eight curriculum-comparison trials, while Table 8 reports recovery frequencies over 20 random model initializations. These are changed reporting designs across different experiments, rather than an established increase in repetitions of the same experiment.

E6.justification: The addition result grids are substantially replaced, and many new task results appear. Asymmetric-function accuracy changes from 90.3–91.0% at N=20 in v1 Table 10 to 95.1–96.2% at N=16 in v2 Table 9; different settings prevent interpreting this as a matched performance gain. V2 Table 8 newly reports 10–20% noiseless recovery with custom loss versus 0% with MSE, alongside new synthetic and polynomial outcomes.

T1.justification: The unit-circle MSE identity is retained. V1's formal g_interval construction in Appendix A is removed. V2 adds a conditional derivation of origin collapse under approximately constant predictions and uniform targets in Section 5, plus a finite-difference definition and claimed bound in Appendix D. These are localized changes to supporting mathematical reasoning.

C1.justification: V1 emphasizes three training improvements, including angular embeddings, and headline scaling to N=256, q=3329. V2 centers two innovations—custom distributions and loss regularization—and changes the headline range to N=128, q=974269. It newly claims recovery of '2x harder' secrets and improved learning on non-arithmetic tasks, substantially broadening the stated contributions.

C2.justification: Regularization is reinterpreted from broadly improving accuracy and consistency in v1 Section 5.3 to offering little benefit on easier addition but helping harder recovery in v2 Sections 4.2–5. V2 adds interpretations concerning arbitrary padding values, repetition, and empirical sample-complexity scaling. Limitations shift toward large N, multiplication/scalar-product failures at larger q, and the need to extend noiseless recovery to actual noisy LWE.

D1.justification: V2 newly provides a code-repository URL, secret-recovery data budgets and recovery instructions, decoder/RoPE specifications, polynomial encoding and output criteria, and curriculum hyperparameter ranges in Appendix F. Reported main-training resources change from eight V100 GPUs and approximately 30 hours per GPU to one V100 and approximately three hours. V1's tail-generation instructions and detailed architecture-selection table are removed.

R1.justification: V2 substantially expands positioning around static sampling versus curriculum learning, repeated examples, optimization failures, and cryptanalysis. New discussions include Bengio et al., Charton and Kempe, and Shalev-Shwartz et al., alongside references supporting the added synthetic tasks and LWE setting. Angular embeddings are more clearly positioned as an inherited technique rather than one of the paper's central innovations.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, related work, and conclusion are extensively rewritten around training distributions and cryptanalysis. The former standalone ablation section becomes exploration within Section 4; Section 5 becomes the LWE application; Section 6 gains task-specific subsections. The appendices are substantially reorganized and rewritten.

P2.justification: V2 redesigns the title block, typography, captions, and table arrangements. The introductory results table disappears, and numerous new comparison/task tables appear. The sampling plot changes from zero-count to nonzero-count axes, the learning curve uses training-completion percentage instead of epochs, and earlier tail/PCA displays are replaced by a noiseless-recovery output figure. Appendix tables also receive new side-by-side layouts.

improvement.justification: V2 substantially strengthens validation through tuned curriculum comparisons with repeated-run reporting, controlled repetition and sample-efficiency studies, and transfer tests on synthetic and polynomial tasks. These address important gaps in v1's evidence about why the approach helps and how broadly it applies. The gains outweigh reduced exact-addition reporting and removed diagnostics, although the '2x harder' cryptanalysis claim remains supported only by noiseless experiments and the revised sampling formula conflicts with Figure 1. The improvement is stronger empirical support, not an established same-setting performance gain.
